correctness.rationale: For any three 1-sites, the distance equation b^r+b^s=b^t forces b=2 with equal successive gaps, and four sites are excluded. Counting empty/single/pair/triple finite supports yields both closed complexity formulas. Isolated configurations of at least two sites form countably many shift orbits, each tending only to zero along its shifts. The first two Cantor–Bendixson derivatives fix zero and the singleton orbit. A normalized radius-R block automorphism fixes every configuration with pairwise marker distance >2R, leaving exactly a finite permutation with finite integer phase-shift data on multi-marker orbits. Every such finite orbit permutation extends to a homeomorphism; direct-product and center claims follow. Uniform-support bounds prove unique invariance and entropy zero; conjugacy preserves n log n leading coefficient. The actual embedded verifier enumerated 98 word cases, 98 independent support-form cases and 192 exact oscillation cases.

value.rationale: The all-size group computation is a natural exact dynamical invariant, not just a finite count. The family is zero-entropy and uniquely ergodic but has automorphism groups containing every finite symmetric group and countably generated free abelian subgroups, while its members are pairwise nonconjugate by distinct n log n coefficients. The base-two triple resonance and explicit periodic second-order profiles quantify a natural arithmetic cutoff. This establishes a sharp structural contrast with known low-complexity minimal/transitive rigidity phenomena.
